newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH PARTIES, SOLIDARITY SHARE POWER IN ALLIANCE.
newsitem.headline: POLISH PARTIES, SOLIDARITY SHARE POWER IN ALLIANCE.

text.p: Poland's Solidarity-led alliance of opposition parties elected on Wednesday its executive body which gives the group's parties and the trade union equal representation, the alliance's officials said.

Solidarity trade union leader Marian Krzaklewski, who also heads the Solidarity Election Action (AWS) told a news conference the AWS coordinating team would maintain a balance between politicians and union officials but he would have a decisive voice in cases of a decision deadlock.

"The breakdown is 50 percent for politicians and 50 percent for the unions...but on issues concerning the election campaign and on specific resolutions if there is a deadlock, the chairman of AWS will have a decisive vote," Krzaklewski said.

AWS runs neck and neck with the co-ruling ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) in public opinion polls ahead of parliamentary elections due around September, with support of about 25 percent each.

AWS elected four deputy chairmen: Janusz Tomaszewski, head of Solidarity's central Lodz region, Marian Pilka, head of the conservative Christian-National Union (ZChN), Adam Slomka a leader of a dissident group in the rightist Confederation for Independent Poland (KPN) and Kazimierz Kapera representing Catholic families' movement.
Pawel Laczkowski, a member of coordinating team, also present said AWS leadership agreed on its support for Poland's membership in NATO and the European Union.
"AWS says yes to NATO and the European Union," Laczkowski, who represents Christian Democrats, said.
But he said AWS had its own vision of the EU.
"We support such an Union, which is rooted in Christian tradition and which is an economic and political of nations, which handle their internal issues in line with their own heritage," he said.
